rule: A use case counts as evidenced only when the same BACH use case runs through the canonical module in BACH and in OCEAN and a referenced old/new fixture test passes in the required parity-evidence CI job. Historic 'accepted' values from bach-parity-baseline.v1.json are not evidence.

use_case_states.evidenced: Old and new implementation produce the same observed state on an anonymized fixture; the referenced test runs green with REQUIRE_PARITY_EVIDENCE=1.
use_case_states.divergent: The referenced test shows old and new differ. Recorded as a finding, never counted as evidence.

row_states.not-evidenced: No use case of this row is evidenced.
row_states.partially-evidenced: At least one use case is evidenced; the row still has open operations.
row_states.evidenced: Every operation listed in operations_in_scope is covered by an evidenced use case.
row_states.not-independent: Alias or access surface; no own evidence.

use_cases.summary: Host A publishes its database to the shared transit directory, host B pulls: newer foreign rows arrive, local-only rows and local secret rows stay, no secret row is published, a repeated pull changes nothing.

implementations.bach_new: the same BACH handler through its sqlite-transit-sync provider seam

use_cases.summary: Target already holds a row newer than every incoming row. Native ProSync merges only rows newer than the table-wide maximum timestamp and drops the newer foreign rows; the module merges per row (last write wins). BACH with the module and OCEAN agree.
use_cases.finding: Native ProSync table-maximum watermark loses newer foreign rows. Not parity; decision needed whether the module behavior is the accepted target.
